nfs_teaching.prerequisite_note: Before this task, use the preceding file/mount lessons: read a canonical path, distinguish saved and live mounts, and recognize owner/group/other permissions. The concepts below introduce the NFS-specific layers before assessment.

concepts.title: Server, client and paths
concepts.text: NFS shares existing files from a server with a client. The export root /srv/manuals/reference is a server path; /mnt/manuals/reference is the client mountpoint. Select only the supplied server, clients, mountpoints and files. The archive is unrelated work to preserve.

concepts.title: An explicit export rule
concepts.text: Write one export per line: /srv/manuals/reference 192.0.2.20(ro). The space separates the root and client selector; parentheses attach options to that selector without a space. An IPv4 literal selects that address; /32 means the same single address. A /24 admits its whole matching network, so it can include an unwanted client. Fresh checks try every other supplied client; they do not establish universal IPv4 access control. The closed model accepts supplied roots, nonoverlapping IPv4 selectors and ro/rw, root_squash/no_root_squash, anonuid/anongid options. Omitted access means ro; omitted identity mapping means root_squash.

concepts.title: Draft, saved and applied differ
concepts.text: Typing changes only the exports draft. Save exports stores that text; Apply saved exports parses and activates the saved policy. A syntax error can remain as bounded draft text; an unsuccessful Apply changes no live policy. Changing a document never mounts a client. Applied policy and live mounts are separate; this simulation refuses an incompatible Apply until affected live mounts are explicitly unmounted.

concepts.title: A saved mount is not a current mount
concepts.text: The closed client document uses six fields, for example: 192.0.2.10:/srv/manuals/reference /mnt/manuals/reference nfs vers=3,proto=tcp,sec=sys,ro 0 0. These are source address and root, client target, nfs type, comma-separated options, then the required zero fields. Save mount document stores it. Mount saved entry creates a live mount. Mount explicit takes the same supplied source, target and ro/rw values without editing the saved document. Saving either document does not update an existing mount.

concepts.title: Numeric identity and existing permissions
concepts.text: A supplied profile contains a numeric UID, primary GID and supplementary GIDs. Directory search needs execute permission on every modeled directory; file access uses owner, otherwise matching group, otherwise other bits. Client ro and export ro independently prohibit writes. A fresh rw client mount must still receive export_read_only here, even if file permissions would also deny the write. Default root_squash maps UID0 and any GID0 to the anonymous IDs (65534 unless configured), retaining nonzero groups. It does not mean every anonymous write is denied: the mapped owner can write a suitably writable file. Metadata is immutable here: choose a suitable supplied profile or export mapping, not chmod/chown/create. No trusted host credentials or full Linux open behavior are modeled.

concepts.title: What Check proves
concepts.text: Check reads actual current files/mounts and runs separate new-mount trials against applied or saved policy. Trials leave your current maps and files unchanged. A denied stage is a real model decision; unsupported syntax or context is a fault and cannot count as denial. The example has different names, addresses and paths. Solving it earns no assignment credit. Preserve archive mount, bytes and saved client document while repairing the real task.

nfs_teaching.prerequisite_note: Before this task, use the preceding file/mount lessons: read a canonical path, distinguish saved and live mounts, and recognize owner/group/other permissions. The concepts below introduce the NFS-specific layers before assessment.

concepts.title: Two read-only layers
concepts.text: The required work mount is rw only when its client mount requests rw and the selected export grants rw. A live ro mount stays ro after saving a rw client document. Unmount it, then Mount saved or Mount explicit. Before changing the export from ro to rw, remove its affected current mount: incompatible Apply is conservatively unsupported by this planner until then, not a statement about Linux handle revocation.

concepts.title: Save and publish in order
concepts.text: Exports draft → Save exports → Apply saved exports controls server policy. Client draft → Save mount document controls the next saved mount. Mount controls a current mount. Write existing file controls actual file bytes. These four layers are independently checked; changing one does not silently perform the others. Inspect the failure stage before making another change.

concepts.title: Numeric permission diagnosis
concepts.text: The work directory has search for its supplied group, and result.txt has owner/group read/write. The owner profile matches UID; the helper reaches the same group through a supplementary GID. An unrelated visitor cannot traverse the directory. Owner/group/other classes are exclusive; the model does not fall through from owner bits to group bits. Choose an admitted profile; immutable inode UID/GID/mode cannot be repaired with commands here.

concepts.title: Root mapping and supported repairs
concepts.text: Default root_squash maps zero UID and zero primary/supplementary GIDs to anonymous IDs. Nonzero groups remain. A mapped anonymous owner may be allowed on a different file; this is not universal denial or authentication. Use the disclosed owner or group helper for this publication. For a supported alternative, rw,root_squash,anonuid=4201,anongid=5203 maps the supplied root profile to this assignment file owner/group. Keep the same Save/Unmount/Apply/Mount sequence, then Write with that mapped profile. A mapped anonymous owner can write; unsquashed UID0 remains unsupported rather than a successful denial.

concepts.title: Publish and verify actual bytes
concepts.text: Read returns existing virtual bytes. Write existing file changes only that supplied file, using the selected client target/profile and replacement text. Typing text does not write it. Publish exactly the assignment message, then Check current contents and access plus independent fresh permissions. Keep archive mount, content and client layers exact. Read-only inspections and unfinished request text do not grant or remove applied credit.

nfs_teaching.prerequisite_note: Before this task, use the preceding file/mount lessons: read a canonical path, distinguish saved and live mounts, and recognize owner/group/other permissions. The concepts below introduce the NFS-specific layers before assessment.

concepts.title: Policy retirement needs a live handover
concepts.text: The old client still holds a current work mount. Unmount it explicitly before replacing its incompatible export policy. This simulation planner refuses the conflicting Apply atomically; it does not simulate stale Linux file-handle revocation. Check requires the old current map absent and a fresh old-client request denied.

concepts.title: Two client documents
concepts.text: Select the replacement client, enter its six-field ro mount line and Save mount document. Clear the retired client document and Save it too. An empty bounded document means no saved entries; editing it without saving does not retire the saved mount. Mount saved affects only the selected client/target.

concepts.title: Restrict the intended client
concepts.text: Keep the archive export unchanged and give only the replacement address ro access to work. A literal IPv4 address or equivalent /32 is valid. A broad /24 can let the old or other supplied clients back in even when their current maps are absent. The goal checks every other supplied client, without claiming all possible IPv4 hosts are modeled. Export line ordering is not a grading secret; supported equivalent policies are accepted by outcomes.

concepts.title: Separate now from next time
concepts.text: Current mount and read rows use actual held maps. Fresh trials start with no live mounts and use applied policy or explicitly saved documents, without changing your current work. Successful reading on the replacement alone does not prove retirement or server ro. A separate fresh rw replacement mount must be denied writing at export_read_only, not merely by client ro or inode DAC. Fault/unsupported outcomes never count as export-admission denial.

concepts.title: Protect unrelated work
concepts.text: Preserve the archive client mount, saved/draft client document and exact file text throughout the handover. Use existing supplied IDs and canonical paths. Identity checks still use numeric profiles, directory search and default root_squash; no host service, account, chmod or file creation is involved.

nfs_teaching.prerequisite_note: Before this task, use the preceding file/mount lessons: read a canonical path, distinguish saved and live mounts, and recognize owner/group/other permissions. The concepts below introduce the NFS-specific layers before assessment.

concepts.title: Two shares, two independent permissions
concepts.text: Work is a writable publication on the editor client; reports is read-only on the reader client. Each export and each client mount has its own ro/rw choice. A ro reader mount can hide a mistakenly rw export; Check also tries a fresh rw mount to prove the reports export itself refuses writes.

concepts.title: Preserve the separate archive server
concepts.text: The archive lives on the supplied vault server, with an existing archive client mount and document. Change only the publication server exports. Preserve vault raw/saved/applied layers, archive mount/client layers/file bytes, and the original reports text. Inspect supplied server addresses rather than assuming every path belongs to one server.

concepts.title: An ordered publication
concepts.text: Edit publication exports, Save them, explicitly Unmount affected work, then Apply saved policy. Save rw work and ro reports client documents separately. Mount each target, choose a suitable owner/helper numeric profile and Write the work result. Saving policy or replacement text does not publish file bytes.

concepts.title: Search and identity are still separate
concepts.text: Supplied owner and supplementary-group helper can write work. An unrelated numeric profile is not made valid by a successful mount. Directory execute/search and owner/group/other file bits still apply. Default root_squash is an ID mapping, not universal anonymous denial. Metadata remains immutable; use the supported profiles/mapping rather than inventing inode repairs.

concepts.title: Partial work is visible honestly
concepts.text: A saved-document mismatch can fail its own row while current maps, reads and bytes stay correct. Check reports actual current rows plus isolated fresh trials; it never replaces your maps or writes a probe into current files. A malformed or unsupported trial is not a successful denial. Review each failed row rather than trusting a prior checked badge.

concepts.title: Use the controls, preserve both contexts
concepts.text: The example uses a separate studio namespace, addresses and message. Fill example fields only fills raw values; use the matching explicit action button to execute. Assignment, example, raw drafts and current files persist independently. Read-only exploration is safe within the supplied model; no real NFS/RPC/host command runs.
